exulta.title: Exulta
exulta.aboutText: Exulta rents stretch tents for events, and this is the second version of their website, now live at exulta.be. A Laravel 13 back end with a React 19 front end over Inertia, and a Filament 5 admin panel the client runs themselves. It covers the full public site — product catalog, tent calculator, case studies, blog and contact — plus the operational side: media library, roles, backups, cookie consent and an automated deployment pipeline.
exulta.featureCatalogText: Tents by category with detail pages, images via Spatie Media Library, and case studies ('realisaties') of real events.
exulta.featureCalculatorText: An interactive tool where visitors set a guest count and seating layout, and get the right tent back with its capacity, diameter and starting price.
exulta.featureAdminText: A Filament 5 panel with Shield roles, quick create, Apex charts, impersonation and a log viewer, so the client manages content without needing me.
exulta.featureContentText: Blog, FAQ, partners, delivery and legal pages, all translatable and served in Dutch.
exulta.featureSeoText: Server-side rendering, a generated sitemap and robots.txt, structured SEO metadata, plus an llms.txt and an AI product feed so assistants can read the catalog.
exulta.featurePerfText: Response caching, and Lighthouse reports per page kept in the repo, so regressions show up as a diff.

vhs.title: VHS Service
vhs.alt: VHS Service website for riding arena construction
vhs.aboutText: VHS Service builds and renovates riding arenas in Geluwe, West Flanders, along with the levelling and groundwork that comes with them. I built their new site from scratch on Next.js 16: an editorial design built around large photography and scroll-driven motion, in Dutch, French and English, and tuned for local search.
vhs.featureMotionText: GSAP and Motion drive the scroll-linked animation, Lenis smooths the scrolling, and a full-screen photo slider opens the homepage.
vhs.featureI18nText: Dutch, French and English on locale-prefixed routes, with language detection, a remembered preference (cookie) and per-language metadata.
vhs.featureServicesText: Seven arena types — from ebb-and-flow beds to GEOPAT, geofibres and cofibres — each with its own page, plus levelling and groundwork sections.
vhs.featureSeoText: Generated sitemap and robots.txt, JSON-LD for the business and its location, and canonical URLs that keep only the production site indexable.
vhs.featureFormsText: A quote form sent through Resend, plus cookie consent: analytics only load once the visitor agrees.
vhs.featureGalleryText: A gallery of finished arenas with a coverflow showcase, a carousel and a lightbox you can use with the keyboard.

stalManager.title: Stal Manager
stalManager.alt: Stal Manager dashboard with horse costs
stalManager.aboutText: Stal Manager keeps track of what two horses cost: one of our own and one boarding horse. Every cost is booked with a date, category and quantity, and split between the horses by percentage. There's a desktop dashboard with monthly charts and reports, and a mobile app built for adding costs in the stable itself, even without a connection. It's a private app: sign-up is closed and accounts are created from the command line.
stalManager.featureSplitText: Each cost is allocated to one horse or split across both by percentage, so per-horse totals stay correct even for shared hay or a farrier visit.
stalManager.featureQuickText: Inventory items carry a default price and unit, so everyday costs (hay, feed, bedding) take one tap on the phone.
stalManager.featureOfflineText: The mobile app caches the last data and queues costs added without a connection, then sends them once it's back online. A status icon shows the connection state.
stalManager.featureInsightsText: Monthly totals, costs per horse and per month in Recharts graphs, and month-over-month insights on mobile.
stalManager.featureAuthText: Better Auth with username and password, sign-up closed, sessions kept for a month on the phone. Every page and server action checks the session.
stalManager.featureQualityText: Vitest unit tests plus database tests against a real Postgres, and a public health endpoint for uptime checks.
stalManager.drupalIntro: Shared Costs is the Drupal version of Stal Manager, open source on GitHub: a Drupal 11 module, plus three recipes and a theme that rebuild the app with configuration only. Working offline, which the Next.js app does as a PWA, isn't part of it.
stalManager.drupalAlt: Stal Manager dashboard in Drupal, built with the Shared Costs module and its recipes
stalManager.drupalFieldText: A field type splits each cost over the horses, equally or by percentage, in whole cents: 12.35 over two horses is 6.18 + 6.17, never 6.18 + 6.18. Views adds the parts up per horse and per month.
stalManager.drupalRecipesText: The app itself (stal_manager), a demo with a year of example costs (stal_manager_demo) and a Dutch translation (stal_manager_nl), on a theme generated from core's Starterkit.
stalManager.drupalAppText: Charts, a monthly overview, a printable statement per horse, private receipts, a CSV download and "add as expense" from the inventory, with HTMX navigation and dark mode.
stalManager.drupalQualityText: PHPUnit (Unit, Kernel, Functional and in the browser) with an axe scan of every page, visual regression tests with Playwright, PHPStan level 8 and about 95% coverage.

scan2talk.title: Scan2Talk
scan2talk.aboutText: Scan2Talk is a wellbeing check-in tool for schools, live at scan2talk.be. Students scan a printed QR poster in the hallway and share how they feel in under a minute — no account, no app install. Behind it, educators get a dashboard with trends over time and can open a private chat with a student who asks for help.
scan2talk.flowStep1Text: Find a Scan2Talk poster at school and scan it with your phone. Its signed link is the only way into the check-in.
scan2talk.flowStep2Text: Drag the emoji barometer from 'Slecht' to 'Super', pick a theme and select the feelings that fit. Under a minute, no typing.
scan2talk.flowStep3Text: If the student wants, someone gets in touch — in the way and at the moment the student chooses.
scan2talk.flowVideo: Video: a student checks in on Scan2Talk, from the mood barometer to the thank-you screen
scan2talk.featureQrText: Printed posters encode a signed URL that never expires. Without a scan there's no way into the check-in, so links can't be shared or guessed.
scan2talk.featureChatText: Token-based anonymous chat sessions with a pending queue, join and close actions, presence pings and rate limiting.
scan2talk.featureDashboardText: Overview, check-ins, students and statistics screens with Chart.js graphs of class wellbeing over time.
scan2talk.featureRolesText: Educator and admin roles via Spatie Permissions, two-factor authentication, user invites, masquerade and a pruned activity log.
scan2talk.featurePwaText: Installs to the home screen and is built mobile-first: signed-in staff on a phone go straight to their dashboard.
scan2talk.featurePrivacyText: No student accounts, a dedicated privacy page, and the dashboard and check-in routes excluded from search engines.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: This page explains what personal data this website processes, why, and what you can do about it. It is my personal portfolio, and I keep the data it handles to a minimum.

sections.title: Who is responsible
sections.text: Robbe Saelens, Geluwe, Belgium. For any question about your data, email robbe.saelens{'@'}telenet.be.

sections.title: Hosting
sections.text: The site is hosted on GitHub Pages. Like any web server, GitHub receives your IP address and technical details about your browser when you load a page, and keeps them in its logs for security. GitHub's privacy statement explains how it handles them.

sections.title: Statistics (Cloudflare Web Analytics)
sections.text: To see how many people visit and which pages they read, the site uses Cloudflare Web Analytics. It sets no cookies, stores nothing in your browser and doesn't follow you across sites or visits. Per page view it receives the page, the referring site, your browser and device type and your country, and counts them without keeping your IP address. Cloudflare, Inc. processes this for me; data can be transferred to the United States under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. I rely on my legitimate interest in knowing how the site is used; you can object by emailing me or by blocking static.cloudflareinsights.com.

sections.title: Error reports (Sentry)
sections.text: When something breaks on this site or in the chatbot, a technical error report is sent to Sentry so I can fix it: the error message and where in the code it happened, the page, your browser, operating system and time zone, and the last steps before the error (such as which page you opened or which button you clicked, never what you typed). Nothing is sent when nothing goes wrong. Reports contain no IP address, cookies or chat messages, and no recordings of your visit; Sentry derives your approximate location (country and city) from your IP address and then discards the address. Functional Software, Inc. (Sentry) processes the reports for me and stores them in the EU (Frankfurt) for at most 90 days. I rely on my legitimate interest in a site that works.

sections.title: Chatbot
sections.text: The chatbot answers with AI. What you type is sent to my worker at Cloudflare (Cloudflare Workers AI), which writes the answer from the public information on this site. Conversations are not stored: they disappear when you reload the page. Cloudflare uses your IP address to limit the number of messages per visitor and processes the messages for me. Please don't share personal information in the chat. Answers are generated by AI and can be wrong.

sections.title: Stored in your browser
sections.text: The site keeps a few settings in your browser so it stays the way you left it: theme, language, and whether you've seen the intro or opened the chat. They never leave your browser and are not used for tracking.

sections.title: Contact
sections.text: If you email me or contact me on LinkedIn, I only use your details to answer you, and delete them when they're no longer needed.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.text: You can ask to see, correct or delete your personal data, or object to its use, by emailing robbe.saelens{'@'}telenet.be. If you think your data is not handled properly, you can file a complaint with the Belgian Data Protection Authority (dataprotectionauthority.be).

glance.title: Privacy at a glance
items: No cookies, no tracking across sites
Error reports without IP address or chat content
No ads, no selling of your data
Ask any time to see, fix or delete your data
